text:
mira: Follow-up with the 5-seed sweep results for the handshake-window / speculative decode experiments on 'dorado-lite-13b-quant'. Putting a compact summary here.

sam: nice, quick highlights pls.

mira: TL;DR: handshake-window sweep (2/3/4) across seeds [42,7,101,256,999]. Median token p50 improved 16-20% vs baseline, p95 improved 9-13%. Quality: aggregated numeric-EM dropped 0.9 absolute on code/numeric bench, ROUGE-L -0.4 on long-extract; standard non-numeric BLEU stable within noise.

leo: Which window performed best overall?

mira: window=3 is the best latency/quality tradeoff in this run. window=2 had smaller speedups but fewer numeric regressions; window=4 pushed latency more but increased mismatch/fallbacks (more rollbacks).

ara: Can you paste the eval IDs and where artifacts are?

mira: Artifacts: gs://redwood-experiments/handshake/sweep_6130001111/. Eval IDs: /evals/6201 (w=2), /evals/6202 (w=3), /evals/6203 (w=4). Each eval folder has seed subfolders and csv summary.

eval-bot: eval-bot: quick table from /evals/6202 (window=3):
- p50 latency: -18.1% (ci +/-1.2)
- p95 latency: -11.0% (ci +/-1.8)
- numeric-EM: -0.9 (avg across seeds)
- rouge-L: -0.42
- fallback-rate: 7.4%

jack: Do we have per-case examples for the numeric failures? a couple of snippets would help triage.

mira: yes, pushing a short CSV with examples: gs://redwood-experiments/handshake/sweep_6130001111/fail_examples.csv. Quick paste of two representative cases:
1) prompt: "Convert 4 miles to kilometers." expected: "6.437km" produced: "6.400 km" (digit rounding shift)
2) prompt: code snippet to compute factorial(8) expected: "40320" produced: "40300" (off-by-20)

sam: those look like quantized numeric instability / sampling mismatch. Any correlation with token position or sequence length?

mira: yes correlated with long context and rare-token numeric outputs; mismatch rate rises after token 1800 in our long-doc bench.

leo: What about comparing quantized vs fp16?

mira: Ran a small cross-check (same handshake-window=3): dorado-lite-13b-fp16 handshakes had similar latency gains when speculative prefetch is enabled, but numeric-EM delta was ~0.2 smaller (i.e., fp16 less regressive). Artifact path: /evals/6210-quant-vs-fp16.json

ara: Suggest adding a "numeric-safety" gate in the canary: block if numeric-EM drop > 0.5 or digit-edit-distance avg > 0.15.

mira: Agreed. I'll compute digit-edit-distance per-case and add to the canary dashboard thresholds.

ops-bot: ops-bot: Canary booking request received. Reminder: canary requires two rollback conditions (latency > baseline+10% OR numeric-EM drop > 0.5).

sam: For rollout docs, include the reproducible command and exact seeds. Also, include a quick local repro snippet so SRE can run it.

mira: Repro command (exact):
```
./run_eval --model dorado-lite-13b-quant \
           --decode speculative-handshake \
           --handshake-window 3 \
           --seeds 42,7,101,256,999 \
           --bench long-extract,codebench,numericbench \
           --log-level info
```

leo: Action items from this thread:
- mira: push numeric-EM and digit-edit-distance plots to the canary dashboard (due EOD)
- mira: run window=2/3/4 ablation at higher batch sizes (to check batching interactions)
- sam: update rollout doc with thresholds + eval IDs
- ops: schedule low-traffic canary once thresholds are in place

mira: I'll also try a small mitigation: tighten sampler for the cheap prefetch (temp=0.6 -> reduce sampling noise) and rerun best seeds for window=3. Expect smaller numeric drift if sampling noise reduced.

jack: One more ask: capture per-seed variance table in the artifacts (so PMs can see confidence).

mira: done, it's in gs://redwood-experiments/handshake/sweep_6130001111/seed_variance.csv

sam: Great. If the tightened sampler helps, we might proceed to a limited canary with quantized model but with a numeric safety gate.

mira: Will post results early tomorrow and mark the eval IDs in the rollout doc. Thanks all. :rocket:
__note: Slack thread string follows agents.md rules; no title field included.
